[[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] | after_party = }} The '''2021 [[Suffolk County Council]] election''' took place on 6 May 2021 as part of the [[2021 United Kingdom local elections|2021 local elections]] in the United Kingdom.{{Cite web|title=Elections {{!}} Suffolk County Council|url=https://www.suffolk.gov.uk/council-and-democracy/consultations-petitions-and-elections/elections|access-date=2020-08-27|website=www.suffolk.gov.uk}} All 75 councillors were elected from 63 [[Wards and electoral divisions of the United Kingdom|electoral divisions]], which return either one or two county councillors each, by [[first-past-the-post voting]], for a four-year term of office. Voters who live in divisions which elect two councillors (12 divisions) are entitled to cast a maximum of two votes, while those living in divisions only electing one councillor (51 divisions) are only entitled to cast one vote. The council is subject to a [[Local Government Boundary Commission for England]] review where it is proposed to reduce the number of councillors from 75 to 70. The recommendations were due to be implemented at this election but were deferred to the scheduled 2025 Suffolk County Council election owing to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]].{{Cite web|title=LGBCE {{!}} Suffolk County Council {{!}} LGBCE Site|url=https://www.lgbce.org.uk/all-reviews/eastern/suffolk/suffolk-county-council|access-date=2020-08-27|website=www.lgbce.org.uk|language=en}} ==Previous composition== ===2017 election=== {| class="wikitable" ! colspan=2| Party ! The ruling Conservative administration made 8 gains across Bury St Edmunds, Ipswich and Lowestoft, but lost 5 divisions in rural Suffolk that it had won four years earlier and was traditionally stronger. The Green Party replaced Labour as the second largest party, and the latter were subsequently relegated to 5 seats. The Liberal Democrats continued their descent after making losses in 2013 and 2017, with a further loss. The Independents also finished one seat lower than 2017.
